subject.title: [Bug] v2026.6.9 QQBot: long markdown reply is split into N independent bubbles (one per chunk), not a single message

question: Should QQBot keep the current one-message-per-safe-Markdown-chunk behavior, or merge chunks into one QQ bubble when the combined payload fits a verified safe byte limit?
rationale: Current source behavior is clear, but the issue and repair PRs request a different visible delivery policy while a member comment says the current split is intentional; automation cannot choose the permanent QQBot UX and truncation tradeoff.

options.title: Confirm intentional chunking
options.body: Keep the current chunk-per-safe-Markdown-message behavior, document the truncation rationale if needed, and close or decline the merge-chunks PRs.

options.title: Land bounded safe merging
options.body: Refresh and land one QQBot fix that merges only live-verified safe-size chunks, preserves overflow chunking, and proves the behavior in a real QQ C2C session.

options.title: Compare candidate PRs first
options.body: Pause the issue decision until maintainers choose between the send-boundary approach in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99032 and the chunker-layer approach in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97829.

recommendation.title: Confirm intentional chunking
recommendation.body: Keep the current chunk-per-safe-Markdown-message behavior, document the truncation rationale if needed, and close or decline the merge-chunks PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: sliverp is listed for QQ channels, authored the adjacent chunking work, and made the by-design comment that creates the product-direction choice.
